answers.why: Israel loves Joseph as the son of his old age and makes him a coat.
Israel speaks to his son Joseph and sends him to his brothers.
Reuben hears his brothers' plan and intervenes to save Joseph.
Reuben tells his brothers not to shed Joseph's blood, intending to restore him to his father.
Judah speaks to his brothers about their brother Joseph.
Reuben returns to the pit and tears his clothes when Joseph is missing.
Judah leaves his brothers and visits Hirah the Adullamite.
Judah takes Shuah's daughter as his wife and sleeps with her.
Judah obtains Tamar as a wife for his firstborn son Er.
Er is identified as Judah's firstborn son.
Judah instructs his son Onan to marry his deceased brother's wife.
Judah tells his daughter-in-law Tamar to wait until his son Shelah grows up.
The woman who dies is identified as Judah's wife.
Judah is comforted after his wife's death and travels with his friend Hirah.
Judah sees the veiled Tamar and mistakes her for a prostitute.
Judah sends a young goat through his friend to recover his personal pledge.
His friend returns to Judah and reports that he could not find the woman.
Judah tells his friend to let the woman keep the pledge he left her.
Judah receives a report about Tamar, explicitly called his daughter-in-law.
Judah personally orders that his daughter-in-law Tamar be brought out and burned.
Judah recognizes his belongings and admits withholding Tamar from his son Shelah.
